title: How to Turn a Crisis into a Creative Opportunity
coreMove: Crisis becomes useful only after calm practice has built a route; when pressure arrives, define the decision, bound the feared loss, and aim the extra energy at the goal.

exampleSpecs.audience: Andriy, a coach changing the message before warmups
exampleSpecs.stakes: The team can treat pressure as danger or as fuel for one clear target.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show high-stakes sports pressure being interpreted through preparation.

exampleSpecs.audience: Dean, a speaker building a route before the room is full
exampleSpecs.stakes: The presentation needs calm learning before the real audience adds pressure.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use low-pressure practice to store a response for later pressure.

exampleSpecs.audience: Isabelle, a product lead keeping a team out of blame
exampleSpecs.stakes: The client call can collapse into catastrophe language or move toward a clear next step.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the root meaning of crisis to shift from dread to decisive action.

exampleSpecs.audience: Camille, a project lead shrinking a vague fear
exampleSpecs.stakes: One rejection can become an endless disaster image unless the worst case is named.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn vague dread into a concrete bound that can be handled.

exampleSpecs.audience: Avery, an operations lead turning pressure toward service
exampleSpecs.stakes: The lobby needs a fast decision that uses energy without spreading alarm.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show goal focus turning arousal into useful action during a live disruption.

exampleSpecs.audience: Tiago, a founder making the pressure less novel
exampleSpecs.stakes: The pitch will carry more force if the moves are rehearsed before the stakes arrive.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use performer practice to show that crisis should not be the first rehearsal.
